raw_response:
I will not spread my 20 mu too thin. With only myself at home, I will keep most land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is what I know best and it pays more steadily with my well water. I will put 15 mu into wheat first, then follow that same 15 mu with summer maize after harvest. I will leave 5 mu for cotton. I do it this way because wheat and maize are the main stomach crops here, and cotton gives me some cash, but cotton takes more watching and more spraying, so I will not plant too much.

For fertilizer, I will start from what I did before and add a little where I feel yield can still be protected. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose grain. For wheat, I will put enough base fertilizer before sowing, then chase nitrogen once at jointing. For maize, I will give a strong base and one topdressing around the big bell-mouth stage. For cotton, I will not save on potash because if bolls do not hold well, the field looks busy but the harvest basket stays light. I watch what nearby farmers do, and if many of them use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed and get a fuller stand, I will do the same. With well irrigation, I will water wheat about 3 times in a dry year, maize 2 times, and cotton around 3 times depending on rain. I will still spray on time because missing one pest window can cost more than one extra drum of chemical.
